After declaring the US-Iran ceasefire dead, Donald Trump proposed a 20% fee on all ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz, only to retract it a day later in favor of vague trade deals with Gulf allies.

The Poison:
By treating international law and global shipping security as a transactional shakedown, the administration alienates allies and emboldens adversaries, prolonging a costly war of attrition.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
The error is WHAT vs WHO. They frame the toll as a logical security reimbursement (WHAT), but it was a unilateral political stunt (WHO) that violated international law.

Social Physics Analysis:
Instead of building a transparent coalition to secure the waterway, the actor used pretexts to justify a chaotic shakedown. This transactional approach increased systemic friction and closed off peaceful futures.

The Trajectory: The Path of Fall into Destruction.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Greater Evil. Erratic posturing accelerates conflict.

The Unavoidable Truth: Transactional posturing cannot substitute for coherent geopolitical strategy.

The Unavoidable Lie: The 20% toll was a serious, legally viable plan to secure the Strait of Hormuz.

The data reveals a total collapse of strategic coherence. Proposing an illegal toll and retracting it within 24 hours is not unorthodox negotiation; it is high-entropy noise masking a lack of viable policy.
